**Closing not-planned — not a defect. The premise was falsified by measurement, and the refutation is the deliverable** (report comment 5448636814; PM adjudication of both open questions = Option A on each).

The three-line summary of what actually happens: HotCRM's pinned `case_sla_defaults` beforeInsert hook reads a seed replay (no userId) as a GUEST submission and `delete`s `resolution`; those deletes were silent no-ops until framework #12396 — inside cloud#1672's bump window — made `delete ctx.input.x` effective; validation then correctly refuses the now-absent field. The logical clincher: the predicate can only FIRE when `has(record.status)` is TRUE, so a `has()` that misread present keys would have refused nothing.

Adjudications:
1. **Hooks over seed replays: no framework change** (the dev's option A, adopted on all four axes). The platform already ships the exact discriminator (`ctx.session.isSystem`), and HotCRM main already reads it (hotcrm PR #1294, merged 2026-08-25 — null assignments + `!ctx.session?.isSystem`, its comment citing exactly this class). Skipping hooks on seeds (B) would silently change what a seed row IS; a lint gate (C) invents an enforcement surface for one measured instance.
2. **The remedy is one line of cloud config**: bump cloud `.hotcrm-sha` (currently `3940736b`, 2026-08-20 — five days BEHIND the fix; `merge-base --is-ancestor d2339bbc 3940736b` exits 1) past hotcrm merge `d2339bbc`. Routed to the cloud chain on #1689/#1672; nothing lands here.

The multi-surface table in the report doubles as a reusable reading: NO CEL evaluation surface in this repo binds `record` to the flat-input proxy — the #12601/#12603 trap work is unreachable from every predicate seam, mechanically backed by a zero-hit grep over every `ExpressionEngine.evaluate` call site.
